- No known history of diabetes — makes new-onset diabetes the leading explanation for otherwise unexplained retinopathy.  
- Fundoscopic findings “strongly point toward retinal vascular pathology” — per note, aligning with microangiopathy rather than macrovascular or neuro-ophthalmic disease.  

[GAPS]  
- HbA1c result — critical to confirm chronic hyperglycemia; pending.  
- Fasting plasma glucose — needed to establish diabetes diagnosis per criteria; pending.  
- OCT of the right macula — required to detect diabetic macular edema, which would explain acute vision loss; pending.  
- Blood pressure measurement — hypertensive retinopathy remains a differential; not assessed.  
- Formal visual acuity testing — baseline quantification missing; limits assessment of severity and later comparison.  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Undiagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus
